name: Exclusion limits on squarks and gluinos from the full Run 2 dataset

significance.note: An exclusion limit; the analysis reports no significant excess over the Standard Model background.

summary.plain: ATLAS searched its full second run of LHC data for the supersymmetric partners of quarks and gluons (squarks and gluinos) and found no statistically significant deviation from the expected background. It set a 95% confidence-level limit: in a simplified model with only a gluino and a massless lightest neutralino, gluino masses up to 2.30 TeV (trillion electronvolts) are excluded.
summary.technical: Search for squarks and gluinos in final states with jets and missing transverse momentum, no electrons or muons (139 fb^-1 at 13 TeV): no statistically significant deviation from the background expectation for any search strategy; 95% CL exclusion limit on the gluino mass of 2.30 TeV for a simplified model containing only a gluino and the lightest neutralino, assuming the latter is massless; squark masses below 1.85 TeV excluded for mass-degenerate first- and second-generation squarks if the lightest neutralino is massless.

title: Search for squarks and gluinos in final states with jets and missing transverse momentum using 139 fb^-1 of sqrt(s)=13 TeV pp collision data with the ATLAS detector
why_it_matters: Squarks and gluinos are the supersymmetric partners of quarks and gluons. The paper states that these limits 'extend substantially beyond the region of supersymmetric parameter space excluded previously by similar searches with the ATLAS detector'.
